experience.reason: The sudden, visceral shift to biological horror ("four small lights press against my ribs") breaks the established psychological and metaphysical tension, feeling like a jarring genre pivot rather than an earned escalation of the theme of loss.

The sudden shift to visceral body horror and the introduction of "four small lights" feels tonally disjointed from the preceding metaphysical grief, breaking the established thematic coherence. It sacrifices the psychological intimacy of the "Voyd" concept for a generic shock value that lacks narrative setup.

The shift to visceral body horror ("ribs are my architecture") feels tonally disjointed from the preceding psychological and existential themes, breaking the established intimacy of the narrative voice.

The sudden, jarring shift to a visceral, body-horror perspective ("she believes her ribs are bone") breaks the established psychological intimacy and abstract tone, causing a disconnect in narrative voice that feels unearned and gratuitous.
